messages.author: 206a28660a5a2302
messages.subject: binomial regression
parts:
I have the following model (from West and Harrison, and Gamerman and  Lopes) that runs fine in Winbugs and I am trying to translate it to Stan.  
#Model A
model
{ for (t in 1:T) {r[t] ~ dbin(p[t],171)
logit(p[t]) <- a[t] + b[t]*x[t]}

for (t in 2:T)
 {a[t] ~ dnorm(a[t-1],tau[1])
b[t] ~ dnorm(b[t-1],tau[2])}

for (j in 1:2) {tau[j] ~ dgamma(1,0.001)
V[j] <- 1/tau[j]}
a[1] ~ dnorm(0,0.001)
b[1] ~ dnorm(0,0.001)}

I tried the following Stan model:
tvp_model<-"
data {
  int<lower=0> T;                   
  real x[T];        ## with NA's removed. 
  real r[T]; ## N is the nrow of original matrix Y[N, T] 
  } 

parameters {
  real<lower=0> tau; 
  real a[T]; 
  real b[T]; 
} 
model
{ 
for (t in 1:T) 
r[t] ~ binomial(156,inv_logit(a[t] + b[t]*x[t]));


  
  for (t in 2:T)  {
a[t] ~ normal(a[t-1],tau[1]);
   b[t] ~ normal(b[t-1],tau[2]);
}
  
  for (j in 1:2) {
tau[j] ~ inv_gamma(.1,0.001);
                  V[j] <- 1/tau[j];
}
  a[1] ~ normal(0,1000);
  b[1] ~ normal(0,1000);
}
"
I get the following error:
no matches for function name="binomial_log"
    arg 0 type=real
    arg 1 type=int
    arg 2 type=real
unknown distribution=binomial
Parser expecting: <statement>
The manual suggests that Winbugs function dbin is equivalent to "binomial" in Stan. Thus, I'm not sure what to make of the error.

Thanks,
Greg
